title: Databases
hook: The web server often isn’t the source of truth — it asks a database, and that can be slow.

steps.caption: Your request hits the app server first.

nodeCaptions.app: Application logic lives here — auth, formatting, business rules.

steps.caption: The app queries the database for the actual row.

nodeCaptions.db: Specialized for durable, queryable state. Often the bottleneck.

steps.caption: App shapes a response and sends it back to you.

nodeCaptions.client: You never spoke to the DB directly — and usually shouldn’t.

takeaways: App servers and databases are different roles with different jobs.
Many “slow API” problems are really slow queries.
Keep databases behind the app — don’t expose them to the public internet.

quiz.question: Why doesn’t your browser usually query the database directly?
choices: Security and logic belong in the app tier; DB holds the data
quiz.explanation: Separation of concerns plus access control.
